title: SOC 2 / ISO27001 Posture Review - Aurum Health
summary: Redwood walked Aurum through SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 posture, Trust Center access, and controls mapping. Customer requested SOC 2 report link, Trust Center read access for their compliance team, and clarification on customer-managed keys (CMK) and HSM. Agreed next steps and a follow-up technical deep dive on KMS/CMK.
topics: Encryption at rest / KMS / CMK / HSM
Data residency and private deployment options
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC 2 Type II report link and grant Trust Center read access by 2025-12-15
Customer to provide controls mapping spreadsheet and top 10 control IDs by 2025-12-19
Schedule follow-up technical deep dive on KMS/CMK integration for 2025-12-18
action_items: Sasha Kim: Share SOC 2 Type II report link + Trust Center invite by 2025-12-15
Miguel Torres: Prepare short tech note on CMK, HSM, and key rotation by 2025-12-17
Priya Nair: Send Aurum controls mapping spreadsheet by 2025-12-19
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Sasha Kim (Redwood AE), Miguel Torres (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Aurum Head of Security), Evan Liu (Aurum Platform Eng), Daniel Park (Aurum Compliance)

Auto-summary: quick SOC 2/ISO posture review. Ask for SOC 2 Type II report link, trust center access, CMK details, audit log retention & data residency confirmation.

[00:00] Sasha Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you blocking time. Quick intro: I'm Sasha, AE, and Miguel is our security/infra SE. We'll run through our SOC 2 and ISO posture, trust center, and then dig into keys and logs.

[00:18] Priya Nair: Thanks, Sasha. Main goal today is to validate we can meet Aurum's compliance gates: SOC 2 coverage, ISO controls mapping, and importantly KMS/CMS? customer-managed keys, sorry - CMKs and HSM support. Also need details on audit logs retention and who can access the trust docs.

[00:36] Miguel Torres: Yeah makes sense. Quick note: transcript might have a few mis-heard words, feel free to call out if anything sounds off. We'll start with SOC 2. Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II report covering infrastructure and our control environment; we can share a redacted report and grant your team read access to our Trust Center where the report and our ISO27001 attestation live.

[01:02] Daniel Park: When you say Trust Center access, can we get a role-based view? We don't want full admin, just read-only to the compliance artifacts and evidence.

[01:16] Sasha Kim: Absolutely. We support RBAC. We'll create a 'TrustViewer' role or add your compliance group with read-only permissions. That role gives access to certs, SOC reports, and control evidence bundles.

[01:33] Evan Liu: How do you provision that? SSO/SAML? We use Okta with SCIM.

[01:40] Miguel Torres: Great question. We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. You can map groups in Okta to RBAC roles. There might be a short setup step where we validate your IdP metadata. We'll send the SAML setup guide.

[02:00] Priya Nair: Good. For SOC 2, we need to map your controls to our risk matrix. Do you provide a controls mapping spreadsheet e.g., mapping CC/SC (common criteria/system and compliance) controls to your implementation?

[02:18] Sasha Kim: Yes, we have a controls mapping that ties SOC 2 controls and ISO27001 controls to Redwood features and documented procedures. We'll share the mapping as a spreadsheet; it's the typical CC mappings and ISO control IDs. Note some control names might be abbreviated in the doc and there's occasional vendor-specific naming -- apologies if it reads a bit terse.

[02:40] Daniel Park: Will that include evidence artifacts or just mapping? We need evidence for a couple of controls around encryption and key management.

[02:49] Miguel Torres: The mapping doc references evidence artifacts in the Trust Center. For encryption and KMS, we'll link to architecture diagrams, KMS key rotation policy, and our HSM usage notes. If you need deeper detail, Miguel (me) can do a technical appendix or a live deep dive.

[03:10] [small crosstalk]

[03:20] Priya Nair: Data residency — Aurum requires EU residency for PHI-adjacent metadata. Which regions can we pin to with Redwood Hosted? And for Private, what's the network isolation story?

[03:33] Miguel Torres: For hosted we have region pinning — EU regions are available and we can run inference in eu-west-1 equivalents; we also support Dedicated pools that are single-tenant and can be isolated. For full control, Redwood Private gives you a customer-controlled environment in your VPC or on-prem with our control plane optionally federated or self-hosted.

[03:55] Evan Liu: If we choose Hosted but want EU-only data processing, do you have contractual data residency and contractual SCCs?

[04:02] Sasha Kim: We have data processing agreements and can include EU data residency clauses; we also support standard contractual clauses and will work with your legal team. We'll surface our DPA and data residency language when we share the Trust Center link.

[04:20] Daniel Park: Audit logs — what is the retention and can we get a copy? We need immutable logs for a 3-year retention for certain controls.

[04:30] Miguel Torres: Logs are retained by default for 365 days in the hosted plan; for enterprise customers we offer extended retention as an add-on and can export logs to your SIEM via a secure forwarder. For Dedicated and Private, you can push logs into your own storage with retention policies you control. We do support S3 export and syslog endpoints.

[04:57] Priya Nair: Are the logs tamper-evident? We need assurances for immutability or append-only behaviour.

[05:05] Miguel Torres: For hosted we maintain chain-of-custody and integrity checks; for maximum assurance we'd recommend exporting to your own immutable store or using our Dedicated offering where you own the logging backend. We can add a note in the mapping about log integrity and provide our logging architecture doc.

[05:28] Sasha Kim: Switching back to KMS and keys — Priya you mentioned CMK. We support two models: Redwood-managed keys (default) and customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS. For CMK, we integrate with AWS KMS or a bring-your-own-HSM model for Private deployments. Key rotation policies are configurable and we log key usage.

[05:52] Evan Liu: Are keys used for model artifacts and for encryption-at-rest of customer data? We need separation of duties.

[05:58] Miguel Torres: Yes, we use KMS for encrypting at-rest customer data and for some artifact encryption. For Dedicated/Private we can support a separate key for each customer and role separation such that Redwood ops do not have access to your CMK. For hosted with CMK, we can set up key policies that restrict key access. There are some operational implications we should walk through.

[06:25] Daniel Park: Any SLA impact if we require CMK + zero-read for Redwood ops?

[06:32] Miguel Torres: Potentially. If we can't access keys for recovery, there are recovery SLA tradeoffs. For most customers we do a dual-control model or emergency key escrow under strict governance. We'll outline the tradeoffs in the tech appendix.

[06:48] Priya Nair: Can you confirm HSM usage and FIPS validations? We need to reference FIPS 140-2/3 validated modules in our audit.

[06:58] Miguel Torres: Our cloud KMS providers use validated HSMs; for on-prem Private deployments we can integrate with customer HSMs that are FIPS-validated. We'll include the HSM vendor/validation details in the Trust Center evidence.

[07:18] Sasha Kim: Quick pause — are there any specific ISO27001 controls you want to call out now?

[07:24] Priya Nair: A few: A.12 operations, A.10 cryptography, A.9 access control, plus evidence for A.16 incident response. We need mapping and recent test evidence if possible.

[07:36] Miguel Torres: We'll map those. Incident response evidence includes runbooks, tabletop exercise notes, and our incident timeline redacted. For cryptography we'll include key management policies and rotation schedules.

[07:52] [noise]

[08:00] Evan Liu: Backups: encryption at rest and key separation across backups — are backup keys the same as active data keys?

[08:08] Miguel Torres: Backups are encrypted with separate envelope keys and we can configure a separate key lifecycle for backups. We'll document that in the tech note.

[08:20] Daniel Park: For the controls mapping, can you provide an index of artifacts (e.g., evidence ID -> path in Trust Center) so our auditors can pull them easily?

[08:30] Sasha Kim: Yes, we can include evidence IDs and direct links when we grant Trust Center access. Links will be permissioned to your read-only role.

[08:42] Priya Nair: About log access — can we set up a role that can only view logs and not modify configurations?

[08:50] Miguel Torres: Yes, we have granular RBAC. We'll add a recommended role set for compliance reviewers: LogsViewer, TrustViewer, and InfraReader. We'll include that in the Trust Center invite email.

[09:04] Sasha Kim: Any questions on encryption in transit? We use TLS 1.2+; certificate management is rotated and we have monitoring for cert expiry.

[09:14] Priya Nair: Fine. On the legal side, do you support a sub-processor list? Auditors usually want to see that.

[09:23] Sasha Kim: Yes, we'll share a current sub-processor list in the Trust Center; it's part of the DPA package.

[09:32] Evan Liu: A quick nit — earlier we saw mention of KV-cache in your docs; is any customer data stored in caches in plaintext? That's a concern for us.

[09:42] Miguel Torres: KV caches are encrypted at rest and we segregate cache namespaces per customer in Dedicated/Private. For hosted we apply logical isolation and encryption; sensitive PII should be redacted on your side before sending if that is a requirement. We'll mark the KV cache behavior in the mapping.

[10:05] Daniel Park: Do you provide signed attestations for penetration tests? We need up-to-date pentest reports or an attestation letter.

[10:12] Sasha Kim: We have a recent pentest summary and can provide an executive summary and case-by-case redacted report under NDA. We'll include the pentest attestation in the Trust Center.

[10:26] [silence 10s]

[10:38] Priya Nair: Ok, so recap of what we need from Redwood: SOC 2 Type II report, Trust Center read access for our compliance group, controls mapping spreadsheet with evidence links, tech appendix on KMS/CMK/HSM and key rotation, and log export options and retention details.

[10:58] Sasha Kim: Correct. We'll do that and also propose a follow-up technical deep dive for Miguel to present details on CMK and HSM.

[11:08] Miguel Torres: For the tech deep dive I'll prepare diagrams showing key lifecycle, who can rotate, audit trail snippets, and the implications for SLA.

[11:18] Evan Liu: Great. Timeline: can we get the SOC 2 and Trust Center access by Monday 2025-12-15? That would let our auditors start the mapping.

[11:27] Sasha Kim: Yes that's feasible. I'll send the invite and report links by the 15th.

[11:33] Priya Nair: One more: are there any known residual risks or control gaps you call out for customers using Hosted vs Private? A short statement we can include in our risk log would help.

[11:44] Miguel Torres: We'll add a short 'Residual Risks' section in the mapping doc. In short: hosted has multi-tenant control boundaries and default log retention; Dedicated/Private reduce shared-surface risks and give you more control over keys and logs. We'll be explicit about operational tradeoffs.

[12:04] Sasha Kim: Good -- any final questions?

[12:09] Daniel Park: No, just to confirm the next meeting for deep dive will be around 12/18 pending your availability.

[12:18] Sasha Kim: We'll propose a slot. Thanks everyone.

[12:25] Priya Nair: Thanks all. Very helpful.

[12:30] End of recording.

References shared during call: Trust Center link (will be provided), SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), KMS/CMK integration guide (tech note to follow), RBAC/SSO SAML guide (setup doc).

Notes about transcription quality: medium — a handful of vendor names may be slightly mis-transcribed (e.g., "KV cache" as "K V cache").
